messages:
marta: heads up — since the eu-central1 cohort migration started ~30m ago we're seeing a slow steady rise in preemptions and a growing placement queue. pods are getting evicted in waves and then queued back causing bursty scheduling and network spikes :grimacing:

simon: saw the same. a lot of the thundering appears to be tiny-gpu jobs that are gang-scheduled with topologyAffinity to az-a. when that AZ started draining, pods got rescheduled into az-b/c but affinity made them fail -> eviction loop.

cheng: logs i pulled from scheduler: 
```
I0320 18:07:12.123456 1 scheduler_predicates.go:312] pod tiny-job-77 failed Fit: PodAntiAffinity conflicts with existing pods in zone az-a
I0320 18:07:14.987654 1 event.go:281] Normal Scheduled pod tiny-job-77 to node gpu-eu-az-b-02
I0320 18:07:15.012345 1 kubelet_evictions.go:87] Evicted pod tiny-job-77: node throttled, preempt required
```
Seems like a combination of taint/affinity + descheduler frequency mismatch.

michelle: current descheduler policy is 15m window and we have drain jobs every 10m for the migration batch. descheduler can't catch up so we get partial moves that keep requeuing. also noticed some nodes had older label keys (gpu-generation: v1) so scheduler picked incompatible nodes then kubelet rejects.

leo: actionable: pause the next migration batch, and run a targeted reconcile to normalize labels in az-b/c. i can push a patch to the node-labeler daemonset to force-upsert gpu-generation labels. sound ok? :+1:

marta: agree. pausing batch now. @simon do you have a quick command to list pods stuck in pending because of topology/affinity so we can triage which jobs to priorityClass?

simon: use this to get pending-gang pods that request nvidia.com/gpu > 0:
```
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Pending") | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests."nvidia.com/gpu"? != null) | .metadata.namespace +"/"+.metadata.name +" -> " + (.status.conditions[]? | select(.type=="PodScheduled") | .message // "")'
```
That filters out normal pending reasons and surfaces scheduling messages.

oncall-bot: ALERT: evictions_count_eu-central1 up 4x in last 45m. Pager duty runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/ops/evictions-runbook

oncall-bot: Next steps recommended: 1) Pause migrations 2) Bump descheduler to 3m for this cohort 3) Open temp warm pool in az-b with small prewarmed instances 4) Tag long-tail tiny jobs with lower priorityClass or preemptible.

cheng: bumping descheduler to 3m now in canary and monitoring. note: descheduler churn will momentarily increase API pressure — watch apiserver QPS.

michelle: i'm going to create a short-lived nodepool (warm-pool) with 8 gpus in az-b to absorb backfill. creating infra ticket INF-4823 and will attach the autoscale hook.

leo: while that helps, we also need to avoid inter-az gang splits. proposal: temporarily disable topologySpreadConstraint for tiny-gang workloads (flag at pod admission) until migration stabilizes. that will reduce cross-zone failures.

marta: good mitigation. also let's add an automatic fallback route in the router: if scheduler reports "InsufficientTopology" for >2mins, route to compatible lower-gpu model variant (non-gang). can product/infra ops handle that logic?

simon: product ok with fallback for batch workloads. for real-time / SLA-critical jobs we should add priorityClass and mark them immortal for now (no preempt).

michelle: warm pool up in az-b, labels reconciled on 6 nodes, descheduler frequency at 3m canary, paused next migration batch. i'm watching pod backlog metrics.

marta: thanks everyone. we'll keep monitoring for the next hour. if evictions drop below baseline and pending clears we'll resume with smaller batch size. otherwise we escalate to infra-engr to tweak scheduler topology weights. :eyes:
